You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content: "374 :     protected boolean isEOFRecord(byte[] record) {\n375 :         return record == null || ArchiveUtils.isArrayZero(record, recordSize);\n376 :     }"

Diagnosis:
The failing test checks that an IOException is thrown on reading truncated entries from a tar archive using TarArchiveInputStream. The exception is expected if the tar is trimmed (corrupted/truncated).

Looking at TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry():
- If it previously hit EOF (hasHitEOF true), it returns null immediately.
- If currently processing an entry, it skips remaining bytes and any padding until the next entry.
- Then it calls getRecord(), which delegates to readRecord().
- readRecord attempts to read a record's worth of bytes (block size) from the underlying stream. If fewer than recordSize bytes are read (likely because of truncated input), it returns null.
- getRecord uses readRecord, then sets hasHitEOF if the record is null or all zero bytes (EOF record). If hasHitEOF is set, it tries to consume trailing EOF records then returns null.
- Therefore, getNextTarEntry returns null when it detects EOF or incomplete input.
- If header parsing fails, an IOException with cause is thrown during TarArchiveEntry creation.
- However, it does not seem to throw an IOException when a truncated entry happens in the middle of the archives but instead silently returns null (i.e., premature "end").

The test expects an IOException when truncated entries occur, but getNextTarEntry ends quietly at EOF with null instead of signalling an error.

From the recent bug reports and current report summary: They also mention that TarArchiveInputStream silently finishes when truncated tar entries or unexpected EOF occurs instead of throwing IOException.

In conclusion, the root cause is that getNextTarEntry() method does not detect incomplete/truncated entries as errors. It just ends reading silently by returning null when it encounters a short read (read less than expected record size) or zero block, instead of throwing an IOException. This causes the test to fail because no exception is propagated.

The skip, skipRecordPadding, and readRecord methods behave as expected. The issue is primarily in getNextTarEntry's lack of validation/exception throwing in case of unexpected EOF due to incomplete/truncated input.

Therefore, fixing getNextTarEntry to throw an IOException upon early/truncated EOF or corrupted truncated entries will satisfy the test and correct this behavior.

This diagnosis aligns with the test code that triggers reading multiple entries from a suspected truncated tar file and expects to catch IOException. Currently, it does not.

No related recent reports suggest different fixes but the third one on "TarArchiveInputStream fails to read entry with big user-id value" shows knowledge of header parsing exceptions, but that is unrelated to EOF/truncation handling in this context.

Hence, the main fault lies in TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry(), its handling of truncated EOF scenarios and silent null returns instead of throwing.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test case expects an IOException when reading a truncated tar archive using TarArchiveInputStream, but no exception is thrown. Examining TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry() reveals that when readRecord detects fewer bytes than the record size (indicating truncated input or unexpected EOF), it returns null to signal EOF silently. getNextTarEntry() in turn returns null quietly without throwing an IOException. This causes the method to silently finish reading instead of signifying an error. The truncation or corruption is not treated as an exceptional condition, so the test's expected exception is not raised. Thus, the root cause of the failure is that getNextTarEntry() does not throw an IOException when encountering truncated entries or unexpected EOF, but simply returns null prematurely, causing the test to fail.

Recommended fix location is in getNextTarEntry() to incorporate proper detection and throwing of IOException upon truncated or unexpected EOF conditions instead of silent null returns.
